title: Cap. X Arg. X open: if after sufficient grace election arose from foresight, the divide would be man’s act under indifferent grace—not a gift prepared for one and not the other
pass_a_gloss: If after sufficient grace administered the election and reprobation of men arose from foresight of these men’s faith, of those men’s unbelief, then the discrimination of elect and reprobate would begin, not through something prepared and given unto one which is not prepared and given unto the other, but through some act under the help of grace indifferently administered, performed by one, not performed by the other. But this is by no means to be admitted, unless we will to transfer the glory of our election from the pure mercy of God unto the praise of free will.
pass_b_english: If after sufficient grace is administered, men’s election and reprobation arose from foresight of these men’s faith and those men’s unbelief, then the divide of elect and reprobate would begin not by something prepared and given to one and not to the other, but by an act one performs and another does not under help from grace given indifferently. That must not be admitted unless we mean to shift the glory of our election from God’s pure mercy to the praise of free will.
source_text: Si post administratam sufficientem gratiam electio et reprobatio hominum oriretur ex praevisa horum fide, illorum infidelitate, tum discretio electorum et reprobatorum inciperet, non per aliquod uni praeparatum et donatum quod non est praeparatum et donatum alteri, sed per aliquem actum auxilio gratiae indifferenter administratae ab uno praestitum, ab altero non praestitum. At hoc nullo modo admittendum est, nisi gloriam electionis nostrae a pura Dei misericordia ad liberi arbitrii laudem velimus transferre.
